meta.title: Low-power firmware state machine and battery-life estimate
meta.tools: C firmware (sleep/wake state machine with an energy ledger per state) on the simulated MCU
meta.summary: A sensor node that sleeps, wakes on a timer or button interrupt, samples, and transmits in bursts: log the time spent in each power state, compute the average current and battery life, and compare with the duty-cycle formula.
meta.problem: A coin cell holds 220 mAh. Will a sensor node last a month or five years — and which state dominates the budget?
meta.theory:
$\bar I=\sum_s I_s\,t_s/T$ and life = capacity/$\bar I$. Currents: deep sleep 2 µA, wake + sample 1.5 mA for 5 ms every 60 s, radio TX 12 mA for 20 ms every
10 minutes, button wake (random, ~20/day) 1.5 mA for 50 ms. Predicted $\bar I$ ≈ 2 + 1500·5/60,000 + 12,000·20/600,000 + (20/86,400)·1500·0.05 ≈ 2 + 0.125 + 0.4 + 0.017 ≈ 2.54 µA
→ life ≈ 220 mAh / 2.54 µA ≈ 9.9 years (before self-discharge).
meta.method:
State machine SLEEP → WAKE → SAMPLE → (every 10th sample) TX → SLEEP; button events from a Poisson process. 30 simulated days at 1 µs resolution for
state changes; ledger accumulates charge per state.

rows.quantity: Battery life on a 220 mAh CR2032
